content.title: About
content.content: Beetroot is a root vegetable from the amaranth family, cultivated in many regions worldwide. Raw beets have a sweet‑earthy flavor and a crisp texture. They are eaten raw in salads and juices, and also used in marinades and side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beets are rich in betaine, which supports liver health.
The deep burgundy color comes from anthocyanins, powerful antioxidants.
Beet greens (mangel) are edible and highly nutritious.
Beets have been used as a natural dye since ancient Rome.
In Russia, beets are a staple of borscht, but they are also enjoyed as raw grated salads.

items.title: High in antioxidants
items.content: Anthocyanins and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Nitrate compounds promote vasodilation and may lower blood pressure.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is essential for DNA synthesis and especially important for pregnant women.

items.title: Supports liver function
items.content: Betaine assists detoxification and protects the liver from toxins.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Beets contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some people may experience an allergic reaction to beetroot.

items.title: Possible contamination
items.content: Raw beets may carry soil contaminants; wash them thoroughly before consumption.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beetroot can be grated into salads, added to smoothies, juiced, or pickled in vinegar. For a softer texture it is often blanched, but raw beets retain the most nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store beets in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, placed in a perforated bag. When kept properly, they stay fresh for 2–3 weeks. Keep them away from ethylene‑producing fruits, which accelerate spoilage.
